error.changed: Run Check > Self-test to see whether the source has changed.
error.moved: The source no longer serves this address; it has probably moved. Run Check > Self-test (ashare-cli self-test) to see which source changed, and send selftest_report.json with a bug report.
error.refused: The source refused or rate-limited the request. Wait a while before trying again; the program never works around such limits.
error.server: The source had a server error. Try again later.
error.timeout: The source did not answer in time. Try again later.
error.unreachable: This computer could not reach the source. Check the network connection, proxy or firewall, then run Check > Self-test.
section.accuracy.intro: Measures how accurately figures are read from documents, against a 'golden corpus' of reports whose values you have checked by hand. The result sets the confidence attached to extracted values.
section.accuracy.title: Parser accuracy
section.actions.intro: Dividends, bonus and capitalisation issues, placements, rights issues, buybacks, cancellations and conversions, read from downloaded announcements.
section.actions.title: Corporate actions
section.board.intro: Who runs the company and how it compares with its industry peers.
section.board.title: Board & industry
section.company.intro: Everything known about one company, optionally as it was known on a past date (only information published by then is used).
section.company.title: Company
section.datasets.intro: Research panels without look-ahead, valuation, and event studies. Every panel comes with a codebook and a manifest, so the dataset can be described and rebuilt.
section.datasets.title: Datasets
section.disclosures.intro: Announcements and reports from CNINFO. Downloading the documents lets later steps read figures, corporate actions and regulatory events from them.
section.disclosures.title: Disclosures
section.financials.intro: Financial statement figures read from downloaded reports. Native XBRL is used where present (high confidence); otherwise figures are read from PDF text (medium or low confidence).
section.financials.title: Financials
section.home.title: Getting started
section.indices.intro: Index membership over time, the trading calendar and suspension days. Index lists come from published constituent adjustments or licensed files.
section.indices.title: Indices & calendar
section.industry.intro: Industry classifications over time (CSRC 2012, Shenwan 2021 or another scheme), imported from the classification lists you obtain. They define peer groups for comparison.
section.industry.title: Industry
section.management.intro: Directors, supervisors and senior executives: appointments and resignations from announcements, and the officer table (tenure, shareholding, pay) from annual reports.
section.management.title: Management
section.market.intro: Daily prices. The public feeds (EASTMONEY_PUBLIC, TENCENT_PUBLIC) are not exchange-authoritative; choose one under Settings > Price source, after 'Test price sources'. Licensed data can be imported from CSV, and is preferred to a public feed for the same day.
section.market.title: Market data
section.operations.title: Operations
section.ownership.intro: Shareholders, pledges, controllers and share capital over time: read from the reports or imported from an authorised dataset.
section.ownership.title: Ownership & capital
section.people.intro: R&D effort, workforce and sustainability information for one year.
section.people.title: People & ESG
section.people_esg.intro: R&D spending and staff, workforce composition and education, patents, environmental and social disclosures, sustainability reports and third-party ESG ratings.
section.people_esg.title: R&D, people & ESG
section.regulatory.intro: Investigations, penalties, supervisory measures, exchange discipline, enquiries, litigation, audit opinions, risk warnings (ST/*ST) and suspensions.
section.regulatory.title: Regulatory & legal
section.research.intro: Search inside documents, trace any figure back to its source page, and produce reproducible outputs.
section.research.title: Research
section.review.title: Review
section.segments.intro: Revenue by industry, product, region and sales model, and the group's subsidiaries and associates, read from downloaded annual and interim reports.
section.segments.title: Segments & group
section.selftest.intro: Confirms that each public source (CNINFO, SSE, SZSE and the price feed) still answers in the shape this program expects. Run it on first use and whenever a collection step returns nothing.

ui.home.intro: Collect data step by step, then analyse and validate it. Every action keeps a record of its source document, so any figure can be traced back.
ui.home.note1: Requests are rate-limited (one per second) and never bypass logins or CAPTCHAs.
ui.home.note2: Public price feeds are labelled as such and are not exchange-authoritative.
ui.home.note3: 'As of' dates use only information published by that date, avoiding look-ahead bias.
ui.home.note4: Fields marked * are required. Leaving a security code blank usually means all companies.

ui.settings.about_note: The same functions are available from the command line as ashare-cli.exe in the program folder (run 'ashare-cli --help'). The user guide, methods document and codebook are in the docs folder.
ui.settings.boards_note: Off by default. When on, 'Update the company list' also accepts these securities, and reads their listing dates from the exchanges' B-share lists and the quote list. Run the self-test after enabling.
ui.settings.bshare: B shares (SSE 900, SZSE 200 and 201; USD and HKD)
ui.settings.contents: Contents: ashares.db (database), disclosures\ and raw\ (original documents and responses), exports\, reports\, releases\, run_log.txt (every action with its equivalent command).
ui.settings.folder_note: Where the database, downloaded documents, exports and reports are kept.
ui.settings.language_note: Pages, actions, fields and messages of this window. Each command's own output, the run log, variable names and files stay in English, so a dataset never depends on the interface language.
ui.settings.locked: Settings are locked while an action runs, and apply to the next action.
ui.settings.price_note: Where daily prices come from: downloads, the backfill and the daily update. Both public sources are unofficial feeds, not exchange-authoritative; their terms are yours to check. 'Test price sources' (Market data) shows which one answers from your network. 'None' downloads nothing: import licensed prices from CSV instead. Imported prices are always preferred to a public feed's for the same day.
ui.settings.updates_note: The program contacts no update server unless you enter one here. The check only reports whether a newer version exists; it never downloads or installs anything.
ui.settings.workers_note: Extraction reads several documents at once, one per worker; the program writes every result itself, so the database sees one writer. 'Automatic' uses all processor cores but one (at most eight); 1 reads one document at a time.

ui.win.ops_intro: Keep the database up to date. The daily update fetches only what is new: announcements since the last run (market-wide, one query per exchange and day), today's prices for all companies, and extraction for companies with new documents. Jobs can be cancelled and resumed; nothing is duplicated.
ui.win.review_buttons: Accept = the value is right. Correct = enter the right value. Not disclosed = the report does not give this value. Defer = decide later.
ui.win.review_intro: Values that need a person's check: validation findings, disagreements between the two text extractors, and low-confidence values, most material first. Decisions are stored separately; the original values are never changed.
ui.win.select_job: Select a job in the list first.
